text: "residential district" shall mean any district described as Village Residential - VR, Residential R-1, Residential R-2, Residential R-4, Residential R-6, Residential R-10, Residential R-15, Neighborhood Model - NMD, Planned Unit Development - PUD or Planned Residential Development - PRD on the official zoning map of the county.
method: Downloaded with ArcGIS REST query (outSR=4326, paged); selected features by attribute; union in a local equal-distance plane; clipped to the Census 2023 cartographic-boundary (cb_2023_us_county_500k) polygon for the jurisdiction's FIPS (sources/geo/cb_2023_us_county_500k) rather than the heavily simplified public/data/jurisdictions.geojson outline, so land near the boundary is not cut off; simplified (Douglas-Peucker, preserve topology), snapped to 1e-5 deg, single MultiPolygon feature. Script: scratchpad scripts/proc.py. Parcel-based zoning polygons dissolved; morphological closing of 12 m (buffer +12 m / -12 m) to fill street rights-of-way between zoned parcels inside a district; holes < 2000 m2 and parts < 200 m2 dropped; tolerance 0.0001 deg.
notes: Result 82.6 km2 = 4.4% of the county. Codes map one-to-one to the ordinance list. The layer is parcel-based, so public road rights-of-way are not zoned in the data; the 12 m closing fills most interior streets but wide highway ROW at district edges may show small gaps (discharge on/across roads is separately unlawful under state law). Town of Scottsville (own zoning) and Downtown Crozet District, Monticello Historic District and commercial/industrial districts are not on the ordinance's list and were excluded. The City of Charlottesville is a separate jurisdiction (hole in the county) and is not covered.

method: Amherst County official GIS (MapInsights 'Amherst_WL_P' FeatureServer) layer 68 'County Owned Parcels'; selected the parcels whose assessor description (MDESC1) identifies a county park: Coolwell Rec Park (125 A 37), Riveredge/Riversedge Park (160A3 A 158), Thrashers Creek Park (49 A 29, 29A, 29B), Stonehouse Lake (50 A 1, 50 A 2), Mill Creek Lake/Park (51 A 12, 22A, 23, 23A, 36A, 36B), Seminole Park (155D A 44A, 101 High St). Monacan Park is county-run on land owned by Eagle Creek Reusens Hydro LLC (parcel 135 A 7, layer 30 'Parcels', legal 'MONACAN PARK'); included. Dissolved per park, simplified 0.0001 deg, 5-decimal coords.
notes: 7 parks. The county's own 'Parks' layer (53) has 7 unnamed, schematic ~35-acre blobs that do not line up with parcels (one sits on private 'Madison Heights Youth Baseball' land), so it was used only to identify parks, not for geometry. Not included: Buffalo River watershed-dam properties (48 A 11/11A/15/16), Graham Creek Reservoir (Service Authority), the county-owned Virginia Blue Ridge Railway Trail parcel (42 A 1) and Leets Spur bike trail parcel (161 A 150), and the old Seminole pool lot - none is clearly designated a county park. Sec. 12-26(C)(4) also bars shooting INTO a park from outside its boundary; this layer does not buffer for that. DCR lists only 'Stone House' for Amherst County.

text: No person shall hunt, trap or pursue wildlife at any time. No person shall use in any way firearms of any description, or air rifles, spring-guns, bow and arrows, slings or any other form of weapons potentially inimical to wildlife and dangerous to human safety, or any instrument that can be loaded with and fire blank cartridges, or any kind of trapping device. Shooting into park areas from beyond park boundaries is forbidden.
method: City of Chesapeake OpenData MapServer layer 16 'Parks' (92 polygons), minus the Great Dismal Swamp National Wildlife Refuge. Ownership was checked against parcels with owner 'CITY OF CHESAPEAKE%' (QuickSearch/MapServer/0; filter in raw/chesapeake_owner_filter.txt). Added 2 city-owned DCR 'Local Park' polygons that are absent from the city layer (River Crest Community Center, a Western Branch Trail segment). Dissolved by name.
notes: 92 features. About 80 of the 91 city-layer parks are at least 90% on city-owned parcels. Exceptions are kept but flagged: Great Bridge Lock Park, Battlefield Park, Battlefield Park South and Deep Creek Lock Park are mostly US Army Corps of Engineers land operated as city parks (they carry a 'note' property). Crestwood Park/Crestwood Middle Fields are School Board land. The Dismal Swamp Canal Trail and the US 17 boat ramp sit on former highway right-of-way with no parcel. The DWR note says the ordinance is for city-owned park property, so the Corps-owned parks are an interpretation. Not included: city 'Open Space Holding' conservation lands and the city-owned 'Gees Group Property' (~630 ac, DCR calls it a Local Park, but the city parks layer does not list it). Separately, city-wide discharge limits in Sec. 46-42 apply.

text: in the northern part of the city beginning at the Chesapeake/Virginia Beach city line at its intersection with Centerville Turnpike, continuing on Centerville Turnpike in a southerly direction to its intersection with Mount Pleasant Road, continuing on Mount Pleasant Road in a westerly direction to its intersection with the railroad tracks, continuing along the railroad tracks extending northward to its intersection with the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway, continuing along the Atlantic Intracoastal Waterway extending westward to its intersection with the Southern Branch of the Elizabeth River, continuing westward to its intersection with Interstate Route 64 and continuing along such road to its intersection with Interstate Route 664, continuing to its intersection with the Suffolk city line
method: constructed from TIGER
notes: Line used: Centerville Tpk from the Virginia Beach line south to Mount Pleasant Rd; Mount Pleasant Rd west to the Norfolk Southern track; the track north to the Albemarle & Chesapeake Canal (AIWW, -76.2101,36.7222); the AIWW westward through Great Bridge to its junction with the Southern Branch main stem, then down the Southern Branch to the I-64 High Rise Bridge (-76.2993,36.7582); I-64 west to the Bowers Hill interchange; I-664 north to the Suffolk line. Area kept = the part of the city north of that line. Doubts: (1) 'continuing to its intersection with the Suffolk city line' after I-664 was read as following I-664 north to where it leaves the city; the alternative reading (straight from Bowers Hill west to the Suffolk line) would add the narrow strip of Chesapeake west of I-664 (Bowers Hill / Hodges Ferry edge) - treat that strip with caution. (2) 'continuing westward' from the AIWW/Southern Branch junction to I-64 was followed down the Southern Branch (which runs north there), not along Deep Creek. (3) The app's city outline is the generalized Census 1:500k boundary, so the northern city edge against Norfolk/Portsmouth is coarse and some real city land is missing at the edges. Within the area, only pellet shotguns on 50+ acre agricultural/conservation tracts with a police permit are allowed (plus the deer exceptions in (f)/(g)).

text: in the area of the county bordered to the north by the James River, to the west by Route 602 from the Willis River, and to the south by Route 45 and Route 684 to the county line
method: constructed from TIGER
notes: Interpreted as the small Cartersville-area wedge in the NE corner: Route 602 from its crossing of the Willis River (-78.1136,37.6854) south to Route 45 (-78.1188,37.6603); Route 45 east to Route 684 (-78.0998,37.6580); Route 684 southeast to the Powhatan County line (-78.0841,37.6472); county line north to the James; the James River upstream (west) to the mouth of the Willis River, and the Willis River briefly back up to the Route 602 crossing. This is the only reading in which all named features close a polygon. Alternative reading not mapped: the lobe east of the northern part of Route 602 (north of the Willis River, up to the James) - 602 does not reach the James there, so it cannot close on its own. The app's county outline is generalized (Census 1:500k) and cuts inside the true James River bank, so a thin strip of real land along the river is missing. The ordinance's other area - all public lands in the county - is not part of this polygon. Rule: no deer hunting in the regular season with rifles .23 cal or larger unless from a tree stand at least 10 ft high.

text: It shall be unlawful to shoot or discharge any firearm, compound bow, cross-bow, air-operated weapon or gas-operated weapon in the following high density areas of the county, except for the protection of one's life or property: (1) R-2 Limited Residential. (2) Gwynnfield Subdivision. (3) Maryfield Subdivision. (4) Daingerfield Subdivision. (5) Shellfield Beach. (6) Richmond Beach. (7) Riverdale. (8) Tuscorora. (9) South Hill Banks. (10) River Oaks. (11) Fort Lowery Beach. (12) Grandview Subdivision. (13) Millers Square. (14) Wilson Acres. (15) Rappahannock Beach. (16) Kaighn Subdivision. (17) Old Howetons Road Subdivision.
method: Downloaded all 10,255 Essex County tax parcels (county ArcGIS Online layer, LegalDescr + TaxMap fields). Matched each name against the assessor legal description (excluding "ADJ ..." = adjacent-to parcels), then used the tax-map page/block that the matches fall on (Essex tax-map pages are drawn per subdivision, e.g. 26C = Gwynnfield) to take every parcel on that page/block. Unioned parcels, morphological closing of 25 m to absorb internal roads, filled holes < 2 ha (not clipped to the coarse county outline, since waterfront lots extend past it), simplified 0.0001 deg, rounded to 5 decimals. R-2 zoning item (1) is out of scope here.
notes: Parcel-derived approximations of subdivision extents (no official subdivision boundary layer exists). Per-name caveats: Richmond Beach: Only 2 parcels carry the RICHMOND BEACH legal description (lots 14-16, tax map 37C block 1). Polygon = all 9 parcels of tax map 37C block 1 (Richmond Beach Rd / Granary Rd). Lies 100% inside the Census place boundary of the Town of Tappahannock; whether the county ordinance applies inside the town was not verified. Low confidence on extent. | Riverdale: Two assessor groups use the RIVERDALE legal description: the main subdivision (tax map 37A blocks 1-3, sections A-C, ~70 lots, Rappahannock River south of Tappahannock) and a small 8-lot group on Summer Breeze Ln (tax map 47B block 1, near Tuscarora). Both are included; the 47B group is uncertain. | Tuscorora: Ordinance says "Tuscorora"; mapped as Tuscorora/Tuscarora Beach (incl. Tuscarora Beach II and the C B Allen plat parcels on tax map 47A). Nearby "Tuscarora Bray 1809" family divisions / Tuscarora Creek Estates / Tuscarora Pines were NOT included. | Shellfield Beach: Includes Upper Shellfield Beach (tax map 38 block 4) as well as Shellfield Beach (38D block 1); excludes Shellfield Landing (separate subdivision). | Old Howetons Road Subdivision: Ordinance spelling "Old Howetons Road"; matched to assessor legal description OLD HOWERTON ROAD lots 1-9 (tax map 44 block 7). | Fort Lowery Beach: Assessor spells FORT/FT LOWERY or LOWRY BEACH; tax map 38C blocks 1-2 (also contains Point Lowery Beach lots 1&2). | Daingerfield Subdivision: Tax map 31D block 1; excludes unrelated Wakefield lots on Daingerfield St (Tappahannock). | Kaighn Subdivision: Tax map 53A block 1 (Cottage Row); neighbouring Neale lots (53A block 2) excluded. | Millers Square: Tax map 49C block 1 (also contains 2 Perry's Place lots). | Gwynnfield Subdivision: Tax map 26C blocks 1-12 plus GWYNNFIELD (PART) boat landing & marsh parcel on map 26. Large lots; polygon spans ~375 ha. Parcel geometries are flagged by the county as being mid-update. Highest uncertainty: Richmond Beach, Riverdale (second group), Tuscorora.

text: It shall be unlawful to shoot or discharge any firearm, compound bow, cross-bow, air-operated weapon or gas-operated weapon in the following high density areas of the county, except for the protection of one's life or property: (1) R-2 Limited Residential.
method: Downloaded with ArcGIS REST query (outSR=4326, paged); selected features by attribute; union in a local equal-distance plane; clipped to the Census 2023 cartographic-boundary (cb_2023_us_county_500k) polygon for the jurisdiction's FIPS (sources/geo/cb_2023_us_county_500k) rather than the heavily simplified public/data/jurisdictions.geojson outline, so land near the boundary is not cut off; simplified (Douglas-Peucker, preserve topology), snapped to 1e-5 deg, single MultiPolygon feature. notes: Result 7.1 km2 = 1.0% of the county. The ordinance (2012) says 'R-2 Limited Residential'; the current county zoning ordinance (adopted 10-11-2022) and the GIS layer name R-2 'Residential, Low Density'. text: Firearms may lawfully be discharged in those areas that are exempted in Appendix J to the Fairfax County Code so long as the firearms are discharged on a Parcel of Land that is posted with signs giving reasonable notice that firearms are in use on that Parcel of Land and that no trespassing is allowed. ... Except for those persons who are on a Parcel of Land that is exempted in Appendix J and who hunt with shotguns loaded with multiple ball shot, it shall be unlawful for any person to hunt with a firearm which has a barrel caliber larger than a nominal 0.224 inches ...
method: No official vector layer for Appendix J was found (searched ArcGIS Online, Fairfax County ArcGIS org services1.arcgis.com/ioennV6PpG5Xodq0, and www.fairfaxcounty.gov/mercator). The text of Appendix J itself could not be retrieved (Municode blocked). Built from the county's official Appendix J "No Shooting Areas" map PDF: rendered at 300 dpi, pink (restricted) and yellow (exempt) fills classified by color, raster georeferenced to the county outline in VA State Plane North (4-parameter similarity fit, median residual ~2.8 px ≈ 170 ft), vectorized; the yellow/pink dividing line was then snapped to TIGER 2023 centerlines of the roads labelled on the map wherever the traced line lay within 250 ft of them (~89% of its length): Leesburg Pike (SR 7), Towlston Road, Sully Road (SR 28), Braddock Road (SR 620), Ox Road (SR 123), Silverbrook Road (SR 600), Lorton Rd connector, Richmond Highway (US 1). Non-road portions (Towlston Rd/Georgetown Pike to the Potomac near Difficult Run; Accotink Creek, Accotink Bay and the east shore of Gunston Cove around Fort Belvoir) keep the traced map line. The county was split by this line and each face assigned to restricted/exempt by majority overlap with the traced map fills.
notes: Exempt area = yellow "Areas exempted from prohibition on shooting firearms and pneumatic guns; however, shooting is subject to restrictions in Fairfax County Code Chapter 6" on the official map: Great Falls/Dranesville area north of Leesburg Pike and Towlston Rd; the strip west of Sully Rd; Centreville/Clifton/Fairfax Station south of Braddock Rd and west of Ox Rd/Silverbrook Rd; Lorton/Mason Neck south of Richmond Hwy and west of Accotink Bay/Gunston Cove. Share of county: 33.9%. Exempt does NOT mean shooting is generally allowed — it is only legal on posted qualifying parcels. Firearm discharge in the exempt area is still subject to Chapter 6: only on a "Parcel of Land" (per §6-1-1; the county wildlife page says 20 acres or larger) posted with signs; no hunting within 100 yards of primary/secondary highways; no slugs; .22-caliber limit except shotguns with multiple ball shot on exempt parcels; no shooting in/within 100 yards of public schools/parks. Accuracy: road-following segments use TIGER centerlines (±~10-20 m); non-road segments are traced from a letter-size county map (±~50-100 m). Towns of Herndon, Vienna and Clifton are colored on the map like their surroundings and are included (towns have their own ordinances). Cities of Fairfax and Falls Church are excluded by the jurisdiction outline. The map is dated November 2018; check for later amendments to Appendix J.

text: that portion of the City south of Armory Drive and Second Avenue
method: constructed from TIGER
notes: Dividing line = Armory Dr from its west end (-76.9578,36.6663) east to W 2nd Ave, then W/E 2nd Ave northeast to its end near the Blackwater River (-76.9185,36.6806); both ends extended straight along the road bearing to the city outline (gaps of only ~40-70 m in the app's outline). Area kept = the part of the city south(-east) of that line, including downtown south of 2nd Ave. Firearm discharge is prohibited city-wide except listed exceptions; in this south area hunting is limited to deer on two of three December days (third Tuesday + following Wed/Thu, 8:30-13:00) or still-hunting deer with written landowner permits (max 6/day, access via private gate road off South St or Amber St); north of the line legal hunting is allowed with landowner permission (shotgun, pistol or <=.22 rifle, 150 yd from buildings/school/park lines). Doubts: the app's city outline is generalized (Census 1:500k), so edges are approximate; land west of Armory Dr's western terminus is assigned by straight extension of the road.

text: It shall be unlawful for any person to fire or discharge any pistol, rifle, shotgun, or any other firearms within the Gloucester Point sanitary district, including any and all weapons which propel a projectile by pneumatic means, as pellet guns or B-B guns, unless said firearm is being fired or discharged while a person is protecting life or property.
method: Gloucester Point Sanitary District polygon taken from Gloucester County GIS "Special Tax Districts" layer (feature SPTXDTDSCRP = 'Gloucester Point Sanitary District'), queried with outSR=4326&f=geojson; clipped to the app county outline, simplified 0.0001°, rounded to 5 decimals.
notes: Area ≈ 686 acres, 0.43% of the county. The polygon is published by county GIS staff but only inside a 2020 sanitary-district analysis web map (no standalone authoritative layer was found; the county GIS server maps.gloucesterva.info was unreachable). It could not be checked against the 1967 plat (Plat Book 4 p.35) and 1973 enlargement cited in the ordinance's editor's note. Shape matches the Gloucester Point peninsula south of the Hayes area, bounded by the York River and Sarah Creek. ~4 acres along the southern shore fall outside the app's generalized county outline and were clipped.

text: It shall be unlawful to shoot or discharge any firearms, including any and all weapons which propel a projectile by pneumatic means, as pellet guns or B-B guns, except for the protection of one's life or property, in the following described area of the county: Commencing at State Route 1301 and the mean high water mark of Timberneck Creek at a public landing commonly called "Field's Landing," thence running in an easterly direction along the center of State Route 1301 to U.S. Route 17, thence running in a southerly direction along the center of U.S. Route 17 to Gloucester Point sanitary district, thence in a westerly direction along the Gloucester Point sanitary district line to the mean high water mark of York River, thence along the mean high water mark of York River in a northwesterly direction to the mouth of Timberneck Creek, thence in a northerly direction along the mean high water mark of Timberneck Creek to the point of beginning.
method: Constructed from the legal description: land (county outline minus TIGER 2023 area water, i.e. York River and Timberneck Creek, approximating the mean high water mark) was split by TIGER 2023 lines for State Route 1301 (Fields Landing Rd, extended ~180 m west to meet Timberneck Creek), U.S. Route 17 (George Washington Memorial Hwy) and the Gloucester Point Sanitary District boundary (county Special Tax Districts layer); the face bounded by Fields Landing Rd (north), US 17 (east), the sanitary district line (south), and the York River / Timberneck Creek shore (west) was kept.
notes: Area ≈ 1862 acres, 1.17% of the county. TIGER confirms SR 1301 = Fields Landing Rd, running from Timberneck Creek east to US 17. The road/water legs are reliable (TIGER shoreline approximates mean high water; US 17 is a divided highway so the line is a carriageway, not the exact center, ~10-20 m). The southern edge inherits the sanitary district polygon's uncertainty (see the gloucester-point-sanitary-district manifest). Applies to pneumatic guns too.

text: Locust Lane Subdivision and the adjoining R-2 zoning district in Midway Acres Subdivision, more fully described in an exhibit filed with a copy of the ordinance from which this section derives in the office of the county administrator.
method: Rebuilt 2026-11 from Greene County's official WebGIS (Digital Data Technologies ArcGIS MapServer VA/GreeneCo_WebGIS): Parcels layer 2 (PIN, legal description REDES1/2, zoning, plat/deed refs) and Zoning Districts layer 25, queried with f=json, outSR=4326 for the envelope -78.40,38.228,-78.365,38.252. Full-resolution parcel polygons replace the earlier geometry, which had been recovered from the 30%-simplified public layer and cut through several lots. Three named features: (1) Locust Lane Addition lots (PIN blocks 60A-5, 60A-6, 60A-7 incl. residue 60A-7-A, plus 60A-3-13 and 60A-3-14, legal descriptions 'LOCUST LANE ...'); (2) the 'MIDWAY' lots on the same road (60A-2-A..E, 60A-3-4/5/6/11A/15/16/17A, 60A-4-7..10); (3) the R-2 zoning polygon OBJECTID 59 (parcels 60A-12-7, 60A-12-8, 60A-12-8A, in the Midway Acres block 60A-12). Lots were unioned in a local metric plane with a 15 m closing to take in the Locust Lane (Rt 1105) right-of-way, holes under 3000 m2 filled, simplified 1 m, rounded to 1e-5 deg. Script: scratchpad areas-recheck/build.py.
notes: About 0.19 km2 (47 acres) at Midway, US-33 west of Ruckersville (38.24 N, 78.383 W). The ordinance (Ord. of 3-13-90) relies on an exhibit held by the county administrator, which is not online, so this is still a reconstruction. Feature 1 (Locust Lane Addition lots 13-14 and 18-54, 29.4 ac) is the most certain part. Feature 2 (Midway lots 4-11, 15-17 and lettered A-E, 7.8 ac) is on Locust Lane and shares its lot-number sequence, but the tax records call it the 'Midway' subdivision. It may not be part of the 'Locust Lane Subdivision'. It is kept in, with a separate name. Feature 3 is the only R-2 district in Midway Acres today (8.9 ac). It does NOT actually adjoin the Locust Lane lots: it is about 130 m away, with B-1 parcels in between. Today every Locust Lane lot and every Midway Acres tract on New Life Drive is zoned A-1, so the zoning map has clearly changed since 1990. The 1990 'adjoining R-2 district' may instead have been the Midway Acres residential tracts on New Life Drive that border the Locust Lane lots on the east (tax blocks 60A-8 to 60A-11: Spotswood Trail Par 1A/1B-2/2A/2B/3A/3B/C, Tracts A/B1/B2, and Midway Acres Parcels 4-7). Those tracts are NOT mapped. Only the exhibit or the county's 1990 zoning map can settle this. Exception (b)(2): discharge on private property with the owner's or legal possessor's permission is not a violation, provided reasonable care is taken to keep projectiles on the property.

text: (a) It shall be unlawful for any person to hunt while on any portion of the Meherrin River which lies closer to the Emporia Hydroelectric Project Dam than four thousand eight hundred (4,800) feet, which is a point generally south of the terminus of Riverview Road. The property on which hunting is hereby prohibited constitutes impounded water of the Meherrin River and real property resulting from the geologic process of accretion which is commonly known as the Emporia Water Reservoir.
method: Built from Census TIGER 2023 AREAWATER 'Meherrin River Reservoir' polygons (Greensville 51081 + Emporia 51595). Dam located at the downstream (east) end of the reservoir, about 36.69595 N, 77.55695 W. Took the reservoir water within a 4,800 ft (1,463 m) straight-line radius of that point and clipped it to the Census cb_2023 Greensville County boundary. Check: the Riverview Rd terminus is ~5,100 ft from that point, consistent with the ordinance's '4,800 ft ... generally south of the terminus of Riverview Road'.
notes: 1 feature (~82 ac in Greensville). Another ~18 ac within the radius lies inside the City of Emporia and is excluded from this county area. The dam point is inferred from TIGER water geometry, not a surveyed dam location (+/- ~50 m). Distance is measured straight-line; measuring along the river would shift the upstream cutoff slightly. 'Accreted' land around the reservoir cannot be delineated and is not included; TIGER shorelines are approximate.

text: upon, from or across any land located within the boundaries of any residential or industrial district as so classified and defined by chapter 24 or any commercial district.
method: Downloaded with ArcGIS REST query (outSR=4326, paged); selected features by attribute; union in a local equal-distance plane; clipped to the Census 2023 cartographic-boundary (cb_2023_us_county_500k) polygon for the jurisdiction's FIPS (sources/geo/cb_2023_us_county_500k) rather than the heavily simplified public/data/jurisdictions.geojson outline, so land near the boundary is not cut off; simplified (Douglas-Peucker, preserve topology), snapped to 1e-5 deg, single MultiPolygon feature. Script: scratchpad scripts/proc.py. Zoning district polygons dissolved; morphological closing of 10 m; holes < 2000 m2 and parts < 200 m2 dropped; tolerance 0.0001 deg.
notes: Result 311.9 km2 = 49.4% of the county (eastern Henrico/Varina is largely A-1, so it is less than 'most of the county'). Henrico's C-1 is the Conservation district, not commercial, so it is excluded. Judgment calls: office districts (O-1..O-3, O/S) were treated as commercial; mixed-use/planned districts (UMU, SMX, CMU) contain residential and commercial uses and were included. Interstate/major-road ROW appears unzoned or A-1 in the data and is left out (discharge on/across roads is prohibited anyway by the same section). Not represented: the section's separate bans on public land/public places/streets; the deer exemption (13-59(b): >=5 ac zoned agricultural; 13-61(d): >=2 ac agricultural for bows) only applies in agricultural zoning, which is outside this polygon. Conditional suffix 'C' and labels with '*' are the same base districts.

text: It shall be unlawful for any person to discharge any firearms or pneumatic gun in the county ... in or within 50 feet of the boundaries of any recorded subdivision ... Recorded subdivision. a. Any subdivision of property into two or more lots (i) which occurred after August 31, 1964; (ii) has a plat recorded in the county's circuit court clerk's office; and (iii) where the new lots created are to be used for residential or commercial purposes. b. The following subdivisions divided prior to August 31, 1964, as shown on the map titled James City County Pre-August 1964 Subdivisions Prohibited from Discharging Firearms, dated September 20, 2011: [57 named subdivisions] c. Any subdivision where two thirds of the lot owners have petitioned the board of supervisors to be included ... d. method: James City County GIS (property.jamescitycountyva.gov/arcgis/rest/services), queried with outSR=4326&f=geojson, paged. method: Hand-built from the §31-28 metes-and-bounds descriptions. Road legs are shortest paths along TIGER 2023 road centerlines between computed junctions. Water legs use TIGER linear/area water and PWC Streams/Hydrology. Other legs use the CSX and Norfolk Southern lines (PWC Railroads), Dominion power lines (PWC Power Lines), Manassas, Manassas Park, Dumfries and Occoquan limits (PWC Jurisdictions), subdivision plats (PWC Subdivisions: Ridgewood Estates), the Marine Corps Base Quantico boundary (TIGER military areas), and USGS NHD named flowlines (Rocky Branch, North Fork Broad Run). "Imaginary lines" were computed as straight lines or as State Plane offsets of the named feature. Each area was plotted over TIGER/PWC layers and visually checked against its description. The result is one feature per area with name and confidence properties, clipped to the app's county outline, simplified 0.0001°, and rounded to 5 decimals. Areas 4, 5, 9, 10 and 11 were rebuilt in 2026-11 from PWC GIS (gisweb.pwcva.gov OpenData MapServer: Subdivisions, Road Centerline, Streams, Hydrological Features, Railroads, Jurisdictions), USGS NHD and TIGER 2023. They were clipped to the detailed county outline and simplified 0.00004°.
notes: Total restricted share of county ≈ 22.8%. In 2026-11 every feature was re-clipped to the app's detailed county outline (TIGER 2023). This removed slivers and three small parts of area 2 (~140 acres) that lay across the Occoquan in Fairfax County; small edge trims also hit areas 7, 8 and 12. Areas 1-3, 6-8 and 12 were otherwise not redrawn. No official GIS layer for the §31-28 restricted areas was found. The county's published "Restricted Firearm Discharge Zone" layer (services2.arcgis.com/0Q7l03Ls62VG0fy4 .../Firearms_Restricted_Zone) is a 100-yard buffer around streets and occupied buildings (§31-23/31-24), not these areas. All 12 areas were therefore built by hand from the legal text, and accuracy varies from area to area (each feature has a confidence property). IMPORTANT EXCEPTIONS (§31-27): discharge is allowed in a restricted area (8) by the owner, immediate family or the owner's permittee on one or more contiguous tracts totaling 5 acres or more; (9) for deer kill permits on agriculturally zoned parcels of 5+ acres; (7) for waterfowl hunting on the Potomac and its tributaries, except the part of Quantico Creek inside the Dumfries/Triangle area; and at ranges/preserves. So these polygons mark where discharge is generally prohibited on parcels under 5 acres. They do not mark a ban on every parcel. Rifles larger than .22 caliber are prohibited countywide for hunting (§31-22), and the 100-yard rules from roads and occupied structures apply everywhere. Several road names and numbers have changed since 1981-2000 (e.g. Rt 234 now ends at US 1 near Dewey Creek). Per-area method and doubts: [1] Dumfries/Triangle (medium): Rt 234 (from its end at US 1 by Dewey Creek) to I-95, I-95 to Rt 619, Little Creek to the Marine Corps Base Quantico boundary (TIGER military area), base boundary to the Dominion power line (PWC Power Lines layer) crossing Quantico Creek at the narrows ~38.548N, power line "inland" to Rt 633, Rt 633 to Dewey Creek, Dewey Creek to Rt 234. Town of Dumfries (PWC jurisdictions) removed. Quantico Creek water upstream of the power line kept only within 100 yd (300 ft) of shore; the open bay below the power line is excluded. Rt 234 now ends at US 1 a few hundred feet from Dewey Creek; that gap is bridged along US 1 (on the Dumfries town line). The gap between S1 and S2 at Leary St is filled. The PWC S2 polygon extends north of the stream (lots on the north side of Gyder Dr) and that part is excluded, because the text bounds the area by the branch. Doubt: the name Felkins Branch is in none of TIGER, PWC Streams, USGS NHD or a web search, so the stream is identified only by fit (it is the only westward-flowing stream between the S1 corner and the west line). If Felkins Branch were the stream farther north through S3, the true area would be larger. [5] Woodbine Woods (low): Rebuilt 2026-11 from PWC Road Centerlines. Start at Rt 234 x Rt 642 (Hoadly Rd) (-77.44064,38.65848); north along today's Rt 234 to the latitude of the Rt 766 (Stillbrooke Rd) intersection; that intersection is on Canova Dr (-77.44083,38.67174), a loop off Rt 234 that looks like the pre-realignment Rt 234 (Rt 766 does not reach today's 234); due west 2,500 ft from that intersection; south parallel to Rt 234 (the chord between the two junctions) to the westward extension of Hoadly Rd's end segment (due west); back east to the start. The text says the parallel leg is "approximately 2,500 feet", but closing on the Hoadly extension makes it ~4,790 ft (the Rt 234 leg is ~4,930 ft), so the text is internally inconsistent; this version follows the closing description. The east edge follows today's Rt 234. If the 1981 description meant the old alignment (Canova Dr/Woodbine Rd), a strip up to ~700 ft wide between Canova Dr and today's Rt 234 (north of ~38.664) would be outside the area. The wider reading was kept on purpose. [6] Occoquan Forest (medium): Davis Ford Rd from its junction with Occoquan Forest Dr (SE junction) west to the Occoquan River; the river shore around the Occoquan Forest peninsula; straight line from near the Bull Run confluence back to the start. Water removed. [7] Manassas north area (medium): I-66 from Bull Run west to Sudley Rd (Bus. 234); Sudley Rd to Balls Ford Rd; Balls Ford Rd to Bethlehem Rd; Bethlehem Rd to Wellington Rd; Wellington Rd to the Manassas city limit; Manassas then Manassas Park limits (PWC jurisdictions layer) to Bull Run near Russia Branch; Bull Run (TIGER centerline) back to I-66. It is all county land in the corridor between the City of Manassas (south and west) and the City of Manassas Park (north and east), using the app's detailed county outline (TIGER 2023). The corridor is cut on the southeast by Russia Branch (TIGER linear water): from where the branch leaves the Manassas limit (-77.44902,38.75547), downstream to where it enters Manassas Park (~-77.4434,38.7606). The area is ~218 acres; it was ~139 when clipped to the old generalized outline. A small strip of county land east of the branch, against the Manassas Park line near Railroad Dr, is excluded. [10] Courthouse complex (high): Added 2026-11. The area is defined as the part of the county lying wholly inside the City of Manassas, so it is the three PRINCE WILLIAM polygons of the PWC Jurisdictions layer inside Manassas (OBJECTID 6, 7, 8; ~39 acres). These are bounded by Lee Ave, Peabody St, Grant Ave (Rt 234 Bus.) and Center St (Rt 28), as the text says. They are clipped to the app's detailed county outline (TIGER), which now contains them (~38 acres kept). TIGER draws the island as one ~42-acre block that also covers the streets between the PWC pieces; the county's own pieces were used instead. Firearms are prohibited on courthouse grounds under state law anyway, and the City of Manassas regulates the land around it. [11] Gainesville area (medium): Rebuilt 2026-11. Doubts: the exact start of the 18,401-ft measurement, and whether "North Fork of Rocky Branch" is this NHD Rocky Branch reach (no fork of that name is mapped). The part inside the Town of Haymarket is kept because the text has no town exclusion. [12] Bull Run Mountain Estates (medium): West of Rt 600 (Mountain Rd) up to the county line, between a line due west from Hunton Ln x Rt 600 (south) and Warburton Dr plus a line due west from its dead end (north). text: It is hereby declared to be unlawful for any person to do any of the acts set forth in this section within the limits of the facilities and lands located within any public park or parkway or lands used by the county for related purposes within the limits of the county; (1) To carry or discharge any firearms, firecrackers, rockets, torpedoes or fireworks of any kind without written consent of the administrator, with the exception of duly authorized law enforcement officials on official duty and with the exception of persons legally permitted to carry a firearm as a concealed weapon, pursuant to Code of Virginia, § 18.2-308 et seq. as amended, while in compliance with any laws or regulations appertaining to such permit.
method: Rebuilt 2026-11. A full owner search of the county's Vision assessment database (gis.vgsi.com/TazewellCountyVA, owner 'TAZEWELL COUNTY', all result pages) found 242 parcels, 59 of them owned by 'TAZEWELL COUNTY (BD OF SUPERVISORS)'. Each of the 59 parcel cards was read for land use, acreage and outbuildings (picnic shelters, bath houses, restrooms and so on). Parcels were joined by PTM_ID to VGIN statewide parcel geometry (FIPS 51185). Two areas qualify. (1) Cavitt's Creek Park / Lake Witten: county parcels 75-A-1A, 75-A-2A, 75-A-3, 75-A-3A, 75-A-4A (757 Recreation Dr: picnic shelters, cabin, bath house), 74-A-143A, 55-A-27A/27B/27C, 55-A-28B (picnic shelter) and 55-A-28C (Mountain Lake Dr), and 54-A-102/102A, unioned with the DCR Conservation Lands 'Cavitts Creek Park' polygon. (2) Tazewell County Fairgrounds: county parcel 94A8A-23 (17.5 ac, Fieldcrest Cir, at the end of Fairground Rd). Its card lists large exhibit/outbuildings, a 3,360 sq ft picnic shelter, a restroom, 47,000 sq ft of paving, a sign and a shop, and TIGER roads show a loop track inside it. Union with a 5 m closing in a local metric plane, holes under 5000 m2 filled, simplified 1 m, rounded to 1e-5 deg. Script: scratchpad areas-recheck/build.py.
notes: Cavitt's Creek is about 231 acres. The fairgrounds is about 18 acres, 0.6 mi west of the Town of Tazewell. Article II of Ch. 14 (Sec. 14-32 (32a)) itself refers to 'the county properties generally known as the Tazewell County Fairgrounds', and the county funds fairgrounds repairs (May 2025 Board of Supervisors agenda). The earlier note that the fairgrounds was the privately assessed parcel 94-A-52 (Peery) appears to be wrong: that parcel is the farmland to the south along Fairground Rd. The county-owned 94A8A-23 is the developed fair site. Still, it was not confirmed on the ground or by the county that every fair-use area lies inside this one parcel. None of the other 46 Board of Supervisors parcels looks like a park: they are the courthouse and office complex in downtown Tazewell, the Lynn Hollow landfill and convenience sites, the airport area, small vacant lots and community or office buildings. Parcels held by the PSA, the School Board, the IDA and the Airport Authority were not treated as park land. School grounds may have their own state-law firearm restrictions, which are not part of this area. Town parks (Lotito Park, Lincolnshire Park and others) belong to towns, not the county, and are excluded. A park the county leases rather than owns would not appear in an owner search. The ordinance also covers carrying firearms (with exceptions), not only discharge.

method: Downloaded all 27,646 Warren County parcels from the county GIS (WarrenGISUpdates/Parcels, which carries tax map "map"+"ins" and a "subdivision" name field). For each lettered item, selected every parcel on the tax map(s) cited in the ordinance (e.g. 23A, 22B, 15E) plus any parcel whose subdivision field names that subdivision; unioned, 30 m morphological closing to absorb internal roads, holes < 5 ha filled, simplified 0.0001 deg, rounded to 5 decimals. Item E (river segment): TIGER 2023 area-water polygon "South Fork Shenandoah Riv" for Warren County, cut at the TIGER "State Rte 619" crossing, keeping the downstream piece to where TIGER switches to North Fork / Shenandoah River polygons (the confluence at Riverton). Cross-checked against Census 2023 CDPs: 95-100% of each subdivision polygon falls inside the same-named CDP (CDPs are larger).
notes: Subdivision items A-D, F-I are parcel-derived from the exact tax maps cited by the ordinance and agree with the county subdivision-name field; boundaries are lot-line unions so road rights-of-way/edges are approximated. Item C deliberately includes all parcels on the cited maps ("and those adjacent parcels") — including Linden Heights on 23C. Apple Mountain Lake West (22C) is NOT cited and not included. Item E is medium confidence: it relies on TIGER naming the road "State Rte 619" at the crossing near 38.904N -78.214W (south edge of Front Royal) and on TIGER water polygons; about 58% of that river segment lies within the Census boundary of the Town of Front Royal. The river feature has ordinance_item "E". Bow hunting by an owner on own property >=100 yd from residences/roads is excepted (not mapped).
